target: route "degenerate" — Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player

findings.defect: A barrier that covers nothing, presented as a general negative result. Its hypotheses -- (ii) 'a block's vertices never switch while dead' and (iii) 'no vertex of B_1..B_{r-1} switches after B_r wakes' -- forbid exactly the offer-and-withdraw / re-entry behaviour that every published exponential policy-iteration lower bound uses (Friedmann, Fearnley) and that rem:closed-now-or-never already identifies as the mechanism. It covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and the audit brief's own rule says such a barrier 'must be labelled as such'. The route labels it nowhere. Worse, the corollary is TITLED 'Gating cannot be superlinear' and its statement ends 'In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1)', which is not what the proof gives -- it is an unproved assertion once hypotheses (ii)/(iii) are dropped, and whether an interleaving chain can exceed m+O(1) is precisely the open question the route was hired to attack.
findings.evidence: degen.tex lines at label degen:cor-gate: hypotheses stated, then 'In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1).' The proof uses (ii) at 'none of them lies in B_r, whose vertices are dead and, by hypothesis, do not switch before round T' and (iii) at 'After round T the blocks B_1..B_{r-1} are at their optima'. The integrator caught this: frontier.tex line ~5249 now adds 'The hypothesis is the point: it forbids exactly the offer-and-withdraw mechanism ... so the corollary rules out one-shot gating and nothing more; it covers none of the mechanisms of Sec:gap.' cor:gate is cited nowhere else in the paper (grep: only lines 5226, 5238).

findings.defect: The clause 'for m = 2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game', with verification sentence 'Both stopping, exact rationals', is NOT verified at the level of def:ssg. The two witnesses are harmonic normal forms with NON-DYADIC entries, so they are not fair-coin SSGs and were never built as such; the route's own builder cannot realise them, and frontier.tex proves no theorem that an arbitrary substochastic rational normal form is realisable ((v4) is on the UNVERIFIED list). Independently, the m=4 witness carries ZERO ties on its run, so even as a normal form it does not exhibit a tied run reaching the ceiling.
findings.evidence: deg_m4_run6.json has Q[0][1] = 362854819/4510476448, denominator 2^5*17*47*67*2633; deg_m3_run4.json has Q[1][0] = 26566357/27305639040, denominator 2^7*3*5*29*653*751 (I factored both). build.py's dyadic_depth is `d=1; while (1<<d)%den: d+=1` -- a non-terminating loop on either denominator. My own exact recomputation from both JSONs: m=4 run [0,15,8,13,1,5,4] length 6 with ties ON the run = 0; m=3 run [6,3,5,1,0] length 4 with 1 tie. The integrator silently dropped the clause: frontier.tex cor:hstar-one's proof cites instead 'the 58-vertex game of rem:blowup-measured (length 4) and the height-6 games of rem:hk-survey (length 6), all nondegenerate.'

findings.defect: The lemma itself (a conditional) is fine, but the evidence offered for its hypothesis (**) is random sampling that never varies the parameter the mechanism turns on. (**) only bites for runs at or near the ceiling; the sample's longest run is 3 at m=4 and 4 at m=5, against ceilings h*_HK(4)=6 and h*_HK(5)=11. The route's gap field states the support unqualified ('feasible on every one of the 4320 runs tested and on the family'). This is the standing trap 'Check whether your instance set VARIES the parameter your mechanism turns on', and the standing rule that 'no counterexample in K random samples' is not evidence.

findings.defect: The theorem is correct and I re-derived its computational core independently, but its stated consequence overreaches: 'cor:seven-two-player holds without its nondegeneracy hypothesis' is false as a statement about what is proved. cor:seven-two-player is about the improvement ORIENTATION; thm:no-seven is about the RUN. A degenerate one-player stopping game whose corner resolution (thm:flat-resolution, corners chosen off the run) lies in the height-seven orbit while all its runs are shorter than 7 is not excluded by anything here. The integrator caught this and added a parenthetical caveat inside thm:no-seven, but the over-claim survives verbatim in the paper's summary.
findings.evidence: degen.tex, thm-no-seven statement: '... and Cref{cor:seven-two-player} holds without its nondegeneracy hypothesis'. frontier.tex thm:no-seven now adds '(A degenerate game whose corner resolution lies in the height-seven orbit while all its runs are shorter is not excluded, and is not what the corollary is about.)' But frontier.tex lines 11702-11706 still read: 'The height-seven orbit is realised by a two-player game on 97 vertices and by no one-player game, nondegenerate ... or not (thm:no-seven)' -- which reinstates exactly the excluded reading. Needs repair.

findings.defect: The route's stated gap is half the truth, and stating only half makes the route look closer to the pivot than it is. Closing 'L <= h*_HK(m) for every one-player stopping SSG' would settle NOTHING about the pivot, because the asymptotics of h*_HK are entirely unknown -- the bound could be exponential, in which case the ceiling is vacuous. The one-player half of the pivot needs BOTH (a) L <= h*_HK(m) in general and (b) h*_HK(m) = m^{O(1)}; or, in the other direction, a superpolynomial-BA-height Holt-Klee AUSO family together with its one-player realisation at polynomial size. The route names only (a). Its own next_steps item 3 asks whether h*_HK is superlinear and then does not spend ten minutes on the cheapest available probe.
findings.evidence: I fed lem:hstar-super's own product construction with prop:hkfive's height-11 5-cube witness (my code /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-sig/super.py, mycube.py, own USO/acyclicity/unit-vertex-capacity-max-flow Holt-Klee tests): (5,1) with x*=1 gives an acyclic USO of the 6-cube, Holt-Klee on every face, BA height 12; (5,2) gives the 7-cube, Holt-Klee, BA height 13. So h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13, i.e. h*_HK >= 1,2,4,6,11,12,13, extending the paper's 1,2,4,6,11 for free. The product is NOT HK-preserving in general: (4,4) -> height 12 non-HK, (5,4) -> 17 non-HK, (5,5) -> 22 non-HK, and (2,4) is non-HK where (4,2) is HK. So superadditivity gives only a LINEAR lower bound on h*_HK and no doubling is known (consistent with solo blowhk.py's 4,9,12).

findings.defect: Unlabelled rediscovery of a textbook device. The lemma's engine is the lexicographic perturbation of a degenerate linear objective (Charnes 1952; Dantzig, Orden and Wolfe 1955 -- from memory, unchecked against the source), plus the standard fact that a generic linear functional on a polytope induces an acyclic unique-sink, Holt-Klee orientation. The route attributes Holt-Klee and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest and stops there; the perturbation device is presented as its own. This is the pattern the project has caught fifteen times.
findings.evidence: degen.tex contains exactly ONE attribution sentence in 31 KB (grep for charnes|dantzig|lexicographic|textbook|folklore|from memory|attribut returns a single hit at line 96: 'Holt--Klee is Gaertner--Morris--Ruest; from memory, unchecked against the'). The integrator supplied the missing one: frontier.tex lem:tie-perturb's proof now says '--- the lexicographic perturbation of a degenerate objective, a textbook device (from memory: Charnes; Dantzig, Orden and Wolfe).'

findings.defect: Folklore, presented as new with no flag. The content is the standard fact that under policy improvement on a reachability MDP the positive-value set grows by at most one backward attractor layer per round -- which is why implementations precompute S_{>0} by graph reachability. The paper already carries the machinery one step away (def:attractor, lem:absorption, thm:kacyclic's attractor sweeps, and the Z_0/Z_1 nested attractor iteration at line 8342, itself flagged 'from memory'). A three-line proof also suffices: the alive set is nondecreasing, grows only when a dead Max vertex first switches to a live successor, and a vertex once alive stays alive, so T <= m; the route's witness chain adds only the first-switch-round bookkeeping that cor:gate consumes.
findings.evidence: degen.tex has no folklore or attribution note on degen:thm-timer. The integrator added one: frontier.tex after thm:zero-timer, 'The theorem is very likely folklore --- under policy improvement on a reachability MDP the set of positive-value states grows by one backward layer per round --- and is stated here because its sharpness matters below.'

findings.defect: Its run-length content restates thm:ladder / rem:ladder. The paper already records that all-switches terminates on L_n in exactly n iterations with n Max vertices; the chain x_1 -> (t0,t1), x_j -> (t0,x_{j-1}) is the textbook two-action chain. The genuinely new content is only the tie pattern (x_{t+2},...,x_k tied at 0 at round t). The route presents the whole proposition as new sharpness.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:ladder: 'The all-switches rule terminates on L_n in exactly n iterations (exact computation, n=1,...,12)'. The integrator added the qualification after thm:zero-timer: 'the run length m itself is of course already the ladder's (rem:ladder), and the staircase is the textbook two-action chain --- its content is the tie structure, not the length.' Also a small mismatch: the LaTeX says T_k has 'no average vertices, N=k+2, a=0', but t_all.py step 4 actually builds the leaky variant (N=2k+2, a=k); the pure form is never run through build_ssg.

findings.defect: A legitimate family but not a lower bound of any interest, and the route's framing ('the growth law', 'measured at five sizes') invites reading it as one. L = m+2 is LINEAR and improves the paper's existing one-player record by an additive 2 at a cost of 113 extra vertices: thm:ladder already gives L = m on N = 2m+2, and a single m=4 height-6 block of rem:hk-survey already gives L = m+2 at m=4. Its only role is to witness that cor:gate is attained -- i.e. to show a dead end is exactly as dead as claimed.

verdict:
FIRST, A PROCESS FACT THE AUDIT PROMPT DOES NOT KNOW: this work is already integrated. Commit 9fafa72 ("... sec:ties (the degenerate route) and h*_HK(5)=11 integrated") added frontier.tex lines 4926-5273 as \subsection{Ties in one-player games}. So question 5 is retrospective, and the integrator already applied most of the repairs an audit would demand: he added the Charnes/Dantzig-Orden-Wolfe attribution, added the folklore note on the timer, added the rem:ladder qualification on the staircase, corrected prop:no-linear-tiebreak's completion counts (route said "24 AUSO completions, 17 HK"; the paper says 96 completions of (S,D), 74 HK, of which 24 agree with the run and 17 of those are HK), silently dropped the unverifiable degenerate-attainment clause, flagged the (**) sampling as "a report and not evidence", and caveated thm:no-seven. Of the route's 19 labels he kept 8 numbered. That is good editorial judgement, and my findings below are against the route AS SUBMITTED plus one residual defect in the paper.

IS IT NEW? Three things are, and I re-derived all three from scratch with my own code (/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/audit-sig/mycube.py, myflat.py -- independent USO, acyclicity, BA-walk, face and unit-vertex-capacity max-flow Holt-Klee implementations, plus my own (F1)-(F4) enumerator):
 (1) lem:seven-flat. Over the free orbit of 384 height-7 outmaps of the 4-cube I get 768 (outmap,start) pairs with a length-7 walk, exactly 4 (F1)-subcubes of dimension >=1 per outmap, and exactly 384 surviving flat structures with a nontrivial block -- one per outmap, a single block, of dimension 1, always containing the start. Exact agreement with the route.
 (2) thm:no-seven / cor:hstar-one. h*_1(4) = 6 < h*(4) = 7. New, correct, and the argument has no shortcut: I checked that in the surviving case s_eps really does equal s' (the unique nontrivial class is the start edge, whose corner is sigma_0, so all other classes are singletons), so the "s' is an LP orientation" step is airtight rather than the slip it first looks like.
 (3) prop:no-linear-tiebreak. Rebuilt from the printed normal form in exact rationals: every row leaks to t0, run 7 -> 11 -> 13, exactly two flat incidences both at x_2 with OPPOSITE actions (sigma=7 action 1, sigma=13 action 0), and y^15 - y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7 - y^5) componentwise with matching zero pattern. The Gordan obstruction is real.
 The 5-cube analogue also reproduces exactly (starts {0,16}; seven (F1)-edges {1,3},{12,14},{13,15},{29,31},{18,22},{0,16},{14,30}; 96 candidate partitions; unique survivor {0,16} at start 0).
Everything else is not new or not a result: lem:perturb is textbook lexicographic perturbation (unattributed by the route), thm:zero-timer is folklore attractor-layer counting, prop:staircase's length is thm:ladder's, prop:partial-lp is a reading of prop:oneplayer-lp's own proof, prop:family is linear.

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle, no polynomial-class claim. But cor:gate is a barrier covering NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and its hypotheses forbid the one mechanism every published exponential lower bound uses. Under the brief's own rule it is "nearly worthless and must be labelled as such". The route did not label it; the integrator did. prop:family is a genuine family per def:ssg (fair coins, out-degree two, stopping, verified from the game at five sizes -- I re-ran t_all.py) but with a LINEAR growth law that beats the existing ladder by +2.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes -- the exhaustive computations are exhaustive and reproduce independently, and prop:res-nonhk is an existence claim for which sampling is legitimate. Two places are not: the (**) sampling (longest run 3 and 4 against ceilings 6 and 11 -- the parameter never varies into the regime where the question bites), and the "degenerate game" witnesses, which are non-dyadic normal forms that the route's own builder cannot turn into fair-coin SSGs and which were reported as "games ... stopping, exact rationals".

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it: closing the route's gap ("L <= h*_HK(m) for every one-player stopping SSG") would settle nothing, because the asymptotics of h*_HK are unknown and could be exponential; the one-player half of the pivot needs BOTH that ceiling AND h*_HK(m) = m^{O(1)}, or else a Holt-Klee AUSO family of superpolynomial bottom-antipodal height together with its one-player realisation at polynomial size -- and on the evidence h*_HK is only known to be superadditive-ish and linear-ish (I measured h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13 by feeding lem:hstar-super's own product with prop:hkfive's height-11 witness; the product is not HK-preserving in general, failing at (4,4), (5,4), (5,5), so no doubling follows).

BETTER OR WORSE? BETTER, marginally, and the integration as made is close to right. Worth their numbered slots, keep: lem:tie-perturb, cor:one-tie, lem:seven-flat, thm:no-seven, cor:hstar-one, prop:no-linear-tiebreak. Not worth numbered slots, demote to prose keeping the folklore note and the "covers nothing" paragraph: thm:zero-timer and cor:gate -- a numbered Theorem whose content is one attractor layer per round, and a numbered Corollary whose hypotheses exclude every known hard mechanism, sit badly beside thm:blowup and thm:gap-equivalence and invite exactly the misreading the paper works to prevent. Correctly already prose: partial-lp, gperturb, staircase, family, res-nonhk, the 5-cube remark. THREE CONCRETE REPAIRS FOR THE INTEGRATOR: (i) frontier.tex lines 11702-11706, "The height-seven orbit is realised ... by no one-player game, nondegenerate ... or not (thm:no-seven)" reinstates the run/orientation conflation that thm:no-seven's own parenthetical disowns -- rewrite as "and no one-player game has a run realising it, with or without ties"; (ii) record h*_HK(6) >= 12 and h*_HK(7) >= 13 beside prop:hkfive, with the observation that lem:hstar-super's product preserves Holt-Klee for some factor orders and not others, since the growth of h*_HK is now the operative unknown and the paper currently stops the sequence at m=5; (iii) if the degenerate-attainment claim is ever wanted, it needs a dyadic witness, not a non-dyadic normal form.
